protocol.instrument_name: NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (UTI)
protocol.instrument_version: Approved 15 June 2026 (no version number printed on the document)
protocol.legal_basis: Approved Medicines are listed in the community pharmacy management of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI) Authority; pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the community pharmacy management of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI) Authority.
protocol.supervision_model: treating pharmacist - 'Pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the community pharmacy management of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI) Authority.' The document does not use 'collaborative' or 'autonomous' terminology and states no additional supervision or endorsement requirement.
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health practice standard for pharmacists managing uncomplicated urinary tract infection in female patients aged 18-65 years in a community pharmacy: four approved oral medicines (trimethoprim, fosfomycin, nitrofurantoin, cefalexin) with a mandatory hierarchical order, an eligibility/consent/referral flowchart, record-keeping requirements, 48-hour follow-up advice, TGA adverse event reporting and My Health Record upload.

steps.description: 'Provisional diagnosis of uncomplicated UTI can be made' (flowchart footer statement). 'Always consider drug allergies and interactions when selecting treatments' (flowchart footer statement).

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'Initial therapy: review the Therapeutic Guidelines approach to management of acute cystitis. As per the Therapeutic Guidelines, discuss option of nonantibiotic therapy (analgesia with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]). Explain benefits and risks to types of therapy. Note patients on non-antibiotic therapy are less likely to need antibiotics; however, without antibiotics, 1-5% are expected to progress to pyelonephritis or sepsis.'

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'If empirical antibiotic therapy is recommended with an Approved Medicine, check first that the patient does not have any allergies or contraindications (refer to medical practitioner for treatment if so).'

gates.criterion: Patient does not have any allergies or contraindications to the recommended Approved Medicine

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: Empirical antibiotic therapy with an Approved Medicine: 'First line - Nitrofurantoin 100mg orally, every 6 hours for 5 days, or / Second line - Fosfomycin 3g orally, as a single dose, or / Third line - Trimethoprim 300mg orally, daily at night for 3 nights. If nitrofurantoin, fosfomycin or trimethoprim cannot be used for empirical therapy for acute cystitis in nonpregnant adult females, use: Cefalexin 500mg orally, every 12 hours for 5 days. Note: the hierarchical order above must be followed for all consultations.'

gates.criterion: The hierarchical order of Approved Medicines (nitrofurantoin first line, fosfomycin second line, trimethoprim third line, then cefalexin) must be followed for all consultations

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'Provide education on non-pharmacological management and self-care including symptom management and when to seek medical care. Educate patients prone to developing UTIs about prophylaxis. Urinary alkalinising agents: efficacy of these agents for the symptomatic treatment of UTI have not been established however some patients find them useful. These agents significantly reduce the antimicrobial effect of nitrofurantoin.'

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient.'

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'Provide follow-up advice and expectations about symptom resolution: Advise the patient that symptoms should respond to appropriate antibiotic treatment within 48 hours. Advise the patient to seek medical care if symptoms worsen (e.g. fever 38°C or higher, rigors, loin or back pain, vomiting) or do not improve within 48 hours. Advise on what to do if side effects of medication occur (e.g. when to seek emergency care, medical review or return to pharmacy). Review the Therapeutic Guidelines indications for urinalysis. Advise the patient to seek care from a GP if symptoms reoccur within 2 weeks after finishing antibiotic treatment, or symptoms develop that are not symptoms of an acute UTI. Where patient has a regular GP or general practice service share a record of the consultation, within a week, with the patient's consent.'

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

steps.description: 'Where GP referral or follow-up is required but the patient does not have a regular GP or that GP is unavailable (within an appropriate timeframe), contact Healthdirect on 1800 022 222 for advice on patient disposition.'

provenance.section_heading: D. PATIENT CONSENT, ELIGIBILITY AND RECORDS

open_questions.topic: Flowchart cell text on page 3 is interleaved/garbled in the text extraction
open_questions.observed: Page 3 line reads: 'Patient has tw s o y m or p t m om or s e of the above No P s a y ti m en p t t o h m as s o (o n n ly e o s n y e m p f o t o th m e i a s b n o o v t e Yes a t d te v n ic d e s if e e s k y m m p e t d o i m ca s l' followed by 'sufficient to indicate presence of a UTI) progress.'. Decomposition testing confirms the question reads 'Patient has two or more of the above symptoms'; the parenthetical note is reconstructed as '(only one of the symptoms above is not sufficient to indicate presence of a UTI)' and the No-branch response as 'Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Provide conservative treatment only. Direct patient to ... seek medical advice ... if symptoms progress.'
open_questions.why_unclear: Overlapping text runs in the flowchart cell could not be separated with certainty; the note wording and the trailing No-branch wording are reconstructions from legible fragments. INC-6, EXC-21 and PW-1-S9 carry confidence 'unclear' on this basis.

open_questions.topic: Flowchart branch labels detached from boxes
open_questions.observed: 'No' and 'Yes' labels, response boxes and question boxes appear on the same extraction lines, with the Yes/No branches separated from their boxes.
open_questions.why_unclear: Step order and on_fail assignments for PW-1-S2 to PW-1-S9 were reconstructed from the diagram layout; branch wording transcribed verbatim.

open_questions.topic: Position of 'Catheterisation' within the contraindications list
open_questions.observed: 'Catheterisation' is interleaved between 'Renal disease, impaired renal function and history of renal stones' and 'Previous episodes of pyelonephritis' in the text layer.
open_questions.why_unclear: The bullet is clearly part of the contraindications list, but its printed position in the list cannot be confirmed; EXC-11 and RF-9 carry confidence 'unclear'.

open_questions.topic: Page 3 has no printed section heading
open_questions.observed: Page 3 begins '(Continued from previous page)' and continues the Section D flow chart and its notes; the page footers 'Provisional diagnosis of uncomplicated UTI can be made' and 'Always consider drug allergies and interactions when selecting treatments' carry no heading.
open_questions.why_unclear: Provenance section_heading for page 3 content uses the Section D heading from page 2, the nearest printed heading for the continued content.

open_questions.topic: No supply quantity, course quantity or maximum supply limit printed
open_questions.observed: The document lists approved oral medicines and dosing regimens but states no quantity to supply, maximum supply or supply duration; these are held in the external community pharmacy management of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI) Authority.
open_questions.why_unclear: max_quantity and quantity_to_supply left empty rather than invented.

open_questions.topic: No form, dose or frequency printed for non-antibiotic options
open_questions.observed: NSAIDs (nonantibiotic therapy) and urinary alkalinising agents are mentioned without any dose, strength, frequency or duration.
open_questions.why_unclear: Empty fields rather than invented dosing; TX-5 and TX-6 record the printed statements only.

open_questions.topic: Mirrored/rotated footer text on pages 2 and 3
open_questions.observed: Footer text is extracted as reversed characters ('.erawtfos latigid eruces gnisu dedrocer eb tsum ... sdroceR') which decodes to 'Records must be stored securely for minimum seven (7) years. The details of all consultations and outcomes must be recorded using secure digital software.'
open_questions.why_unclear: Reconstructed by reversing the extracted characters; wording should be checked against the printed page.

open_questions.topic: Degree symbol split across lines in follow-up advice
open_questions.observed: Page 3 extracts as 'seek medical care if symptoms worsen (e.g. fever 38 C or higher, rigors, loin or back pain, vomiting)' with the degree symbol '°' printed on the following extraction line.
open_questions.why_unclear: Transcribed as '38°C' matching the flowchart wording 'fever >38°C' on page 2; both readings recorded here.

open_questions.topic: Gates where the document does not state the consequence
open_questions.observed: PW-1-S8 ('if clinically appropriate') and PW-1-S10 (informed consent) use on_fail 'unclear'; the flow chart states the requirement but not what happens when it is not met. PW-1-S9 uses on_fail 'REFER' although its No-branch wording is partly garbled.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires 'unclear' plus an open question where the document does not dictate the branch; branch assignments for PW-1-S2 to PW-1-S6 were taken from the printed No/Yes response boxes.

open_questions.topic: Age bounds endpoints not stated explicitly
open_questions.observed: 'Aged 18-65 years' is printed without stating whether 18 and 65 are inclusive.
open_questions.why_unclear: age_bounds recorded as min 18 / max 65 (inclusive reading); an alternative exclusive reading is possible.

open_questions.observed: The document cites the Therapeutic Guidelines and the UTI Authority in prose but prints no reference list.
open_questions.why_unclear: references left empty because the document genuinely has none.

open_questions.observed: referral.routine quotes from pages 2 and 3; urgent from page 3; emergency from page 2.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires one shared provenance object for the referral block using the first page; page range recorded here.

open_questions.observed: TGA adverse event reporting and notification of the patient's usual GP are on page 1; the My Health Record upload requirement is on page 3.
open_questions.why_unclear: Shared provenance uses the first page (1) per spec; range recorded here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verify the community pharmacy management of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI) Authority: approved oral medicines, formulations/strengths, quantity limits and any subsequent amendments.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The Approved Medicines list, formulations and supply limits are held in an external Authority document not included in this protocol PDF; no quantities or forms are printed here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm each pharmacist using the module holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and has successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the UTI Authority.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Training requirements are detailed in an external Authority document; pharmacist authorisation to practise under the standard must be verified locally.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local process for TGA adverse event reporting via https://aems.tga.gov.au/ and notification of the patient's usual general practitioner.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Reporting is directed 'via the usual processes', which is left to local policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local secure digital recording system and minimum seven (7) year record retention arrangements for all consultations and outcomes.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Documentation, storage and retention requirements are stated but the systems and process are left to local pharmacy policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm My Health Record upload workflow and patient opt-out handling for each supply.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Upload requirement is stated but the operational process is left to the pharmacy's local workflow.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local referral pathway arrangements, including Healthdirect on 1800 022 222 disposition advice where the patient has no regular GP or the GP is unavailable.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Referral destinations and appointment routes are not specified beyond the Healthdirect phone number.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how the mandatory hierarchical order (nitrofurantoin first line, fosfomycin second line, trimethoprim third line, then cefalexin only when the first three cannot be used in nonpregnant adult females) is enforced in the prescribing module.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document states the order 'must be followed for all consultations' but does not state the consequence of a deviation (mapped to on_fail STOP).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local policy for patients with multidrug-resistance/STI risk factors, SGLT2 inhibitor use or an IUD in situ for more than 3 months, where the standard allows 'conservative measures or antibiotic treatment, if clinically appropriate' followed by GP review.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clinical discretion is explicitly left to the pharmacist ('if clinically appropriate'), which is a local policy/governance decision.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how the Female* eligibility gate (including the footnote that 'female' includes all people presumed female at birth) and the 'medical or surgical gender affirming care that impacts urinary tract function' contraindication are applied under local policy.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Eligibility definitions and gender-affirming care exclusions are jurisdictionally sensitive and should be confirmed against current NSW Health guidance before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the no-branch wording of the 'two or more symptoms' flowchart cell (text layer is interleaved) against the printed PDF before the rule is automated.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The trailing No-branch instruction could not be transcribed with certainty from the text extraction; the reconstructed wording drives EXC-21 / PW-1-S9.
